tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Degeneracy is model-family-dependent, not scale-dependent.}
Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuned on Few-NERD achieves higher greedy F1 than Qwen3-8B ($.784$ vs.\ $.748$) yet exhibits $2.4{\times}$ the degeneracy ($31.7$\% vs.\ $13.0$\%; Table~\ref{tab:scale_comparison}), and construction fails ($-0.11$\,pp, n.s.). Combined with epoch ablations (3$\to$5 epochs triples degeneracy; \S\ref{sec:fewnerd}) and the cross-regime comparison (Qwen2.5-72B ZS: $46.2$\%, $-0.20$\,pp), this shows degeneracy is shaped by model family and training dynamics, not parameter count alone. Practitioners should measure degeneracy post-hoc rather than predict it from scale.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Degeneracy is model-family-dependent, not scale-dependent.}
Qwen2.5 exhibits systematically higher degeneracy than Qwen3 on Few-NERD across all tested scales (7B--72B: $31.7$--$46.2$\% vs.\ Qwen3-8B: $13.0$\%; Table~\ref{tab:scale_comparison}), confirming that degeneracy is shaped by architecture and training recipe rather than parameter count alone. Construction fails for all Qwen2.5 configurations on Few-NERD ($-0.11$\,pp 7B FT, $-0.20$\,pp 72B ZS; both n.s.), despite Qwen2.5-7B achieving higher greedy F1 than Qwen3-8B ($.784$ vs.\ $.748$). Epoch ablations reinforce this: 3$\to$5 epochs triples degeneracy within the same model (\S\ref{sec:fewnerd}). Practitioners should measure degeneracy post-hoc rather than predict it from scale.

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Self-consistency (majority voting over multiple samples) yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}, and test-time compute scaling has emerged as a complementary axis to model scaling \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
4	But named entity recognition (NER) poses a structurally different challenge: the output is a \textit{set} of entities, two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical sets, and there is no obvious majority to vote on.
5	
6	Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated \textit{quality estimation} (which inputs does the model handle reliably?) with \textit{sample selection} (which of $N$ outputs is best?).
7	Existing self-consistency methods \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, chen2024usc, taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty} assume outputs can be grouped by equivalence, an assumption that breaks for entity sets with partial overlap.
8	Unlike \citet{yao2026consistency}, who demonstrate that self-consistency correlates with task accuracy, we provide the first systematic empirical characterization of \textit{when and why} LP-based selection succeeds or fails for structured prediction, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as the two blocking mechanisms.
9	Our experiments use fine-tuned models, the dominant deployment paradigm for production NER, and separate quality estimation from best-of-$N$ selection.
10	
11	A key distinction structures our analysis: four of five signals (Soft Jaccard, voting confidence, Fleiss' $\kappa$, exact match) are instance-level aggregates that assign identical scores to all $N$ candidates for a given input; only log-probability (LP) is natively per-sample.
12	All signals achieve reliable quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82; Figure~\ref{fig:overview}), supporting selective prediction.

1	\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}
2	
3	\paragraph{Self-consistency and test-time scaling.}
4	Self-consistency \cite{wang2023selfconsistency} improves reasoning via majority voting; extensions handle free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}.
5	Test-time scaling studies \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys} and reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} rely on answer-level agreement.
6	Adaptive variants gate on answer agreement \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive}, input difficulty \cite{wang2025make, feng2025optimal}, or response confidence \cite{kim2026reasc}; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose SC failure modes without proposing gating.
7	All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different gating signals because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.
8	
9	\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
10	\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
11	CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
12	Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
13	Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
14	LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Self-consistency yields large gains on discrete-answer tasks, but named entity recognition (NER) produces \textit{sets} of entities with partial overlap, where no majority vote analog exists.
3	We evaluate five confidence signals for quality estimation (QE) and sample selection on four NER benchmarks across fine-tuned 4B\textendash 8B and zero-shot 72B models.
4	All signals achieve reliable QE ($\rho$ up to 0.45 on CoNLL-2003, area under the ROC curve [AUROC] up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp F1 at 80\% coverage).
5	For instance-level selection, log-probability (LP) succeeds only where LP-quality alignment is strong, and gains are absent elsewhere despite large oracle headroom (the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}).
6	We identify three qualitative factors: instance degeneracy, oracle headroom, and LP-quality alignment; the gap persists at 72B zero-shot scale, confirming it is a structural property of the task rather than a fine-tuning artifact.
7	The diagnostic naturally motivates entity-level \textit{construction}, adapting entity voting to stochastic sampling: LP-weighted aggregation improves F1 by $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC under fine-tuning (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$). Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment.
8	\end{abstract}
9

1	\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	Single-metric evaluation risks selecting the wrong signal; effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.
4	Three factors constrain selection: degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), limited headroom, and LP compression ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667); within non-degenerate instances, MBR utility correlates with F1 ($\rho{=}0.524$) \cite{eikema2022sampling}.
5	Where compression is mitigated (LP range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), LP yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}), though $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ is post-hoc ($p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.14$; Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).
6	Temperature disentangles degeneracy from alignment: at $T{=}1.2$, degeneracy drops to 14.9\% yet LP does not improve ($\rho{=}0.225$; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}); the selection window narrows with model improvement \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, snell2025scaling}.
7	
8	\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
9	Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms (Table~\ref{tab:entity_construction}). Degeneracy gates effectiveness: across seven conditions spanning two model families, two prompting regimes, and three datasets, gains are positive when degeneracy ${<}22$\% (Q3-8B FT Few-NERD $13.0$\%, Q3-8B FT SciERC $17.8$\%, Q2.5-72B ZS SciERC $21.0$\%; all $p{<}0.01$) and absent when ${>}31$\% (Q2.5-7B FT Few-NERD $31.7$\%, Q2.5-72B ZS Few-NERD $46.2$\%, Q3-8B FT/Q2.5-72B ZS CoNLL). Epoch ablations confirm within-dataset ($11.1{\to}31.3$\% degeneracy halves LP gains; Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}). However, under 72B few-shot, construction fails on SciERC ($-0.08$\,pp) despite low degeneracy, indicating that few-shot demonstrations alter the diversity structure in ways that undermine entity-level voting, though the precise mechanism---which is not simple error correlation (Appendix~\ref{app:fs_error})---warrants further study. 1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	Five confidence signals achieve reliable NER quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp at 80\% coverage). Instance-level selection fails due to degeneracy and LP compression---a structural property that persists at 72B zero-shot scale. ## Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling

The paper explores inference compute as another axis for scaling by repeatedly sampling candidate solutions from a model. Across multiple tasks and models, coverage—the fraction of problems solved by any generated sample—scales with the number of samples over four orders of magnitude.

The relationship between coverage and the number of samples is often log-linear and can be modeled with an exponentiated power law, suggesting the existence of inference-time scaling laws.

## Test-Time Scaling Overview

Test-time scaling (TTS) refers to the strategy of trading more computational resources for more predictive accuracy at inference time. The most classic example of test-time scaling is the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) technique, which sequentially generates a number of intermediate textual tokens describing the thinking process before predicting the final answer.

## Recent Developments (2024-2025)

From 2022 to 2023, researchers emphasized structured inference to guide LLMs in generating more complex solutions. In 2024, methods like PRM and MCTS enabled the automatic supervision of intricate reasoning trajectories, yielding richly annotated data for fine-tuning and improving TTS performance.

[写作进展] C1 Test-Time Scaling 叙事重构 — Outline 请求审批

## 叙事核心转变

**当前 framing**: "Self-consistency for NER" — 从 SC 技术出发，发现 correlation-selection gap
**新 framing**: "Test-time compute scaling for structured prediction" — 从 TTS 革命出发（o1/o3, Snell et al., Brown et al.），问"TTS 在 structured output 上是否有效？"，给出诊断框架

**定位句**: "We provide the first systematic empirical study of when and why test-time compute scaling—via repeated sampling and aggregation—succeeds or fails for structured prediction."

## 引用验证状态

- Snell et al. 2024 (arXiv:2408.03314) ✓ — "Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally"
- Brown et al. 2024 (arXiv:2407.21787) ✓ — "Large Language Monkeys"
- s1: Muennighoff et al. 2025 (arXiv:2501.19393, EMNLP 2025) ✓
- o1/o3: OpenAI 产品，引用技术博客/report
- 已在 paper 中的 `snell2025scaling`, `brown2024monkeys` cite keys 可复用

## 受影响章节 + 改动策略

### 1. Abstract（8行 → ~8行，等长替换）
- 开头从 "Self-consistency yields large gains on discrete-answer tasks" → "Test-time compute scaling—repeated sampling with selection or aggregation—yields large gains on reasoning and code generation"
- 结尾不变（construction 结果）
- 增加一句 positioning: "the first systematic diagnosis of test-time scaling failure modes for structured prediction"

### 2. Introduction（45行 → ~48行，+3行预算）
**结构调整**：
- **P1 (新 hook)**: TTS 革命：o1/o3 通过 iterative reasoning，SC 通过 repeated sampling + voting，BoN 通过 verifier-guided selection。在 reasoning/code/math 上大获成功。但所有证据集中在 discrete-answer 或 verifiable tasks。（当前 P1 的 SC 开场融入此段，不另起段）
- **P2 (结构化输出的挑战 — C2)**: NER 输出是 entity *set*，partial overlap，无 equivalence class，无 execution-based verifier。这使 TTS 面临根本不同的挑战（= 当前 P1 后半 + P2 合并压缩）
- **P3-P7**: 基本不变（key distinction, results, gap definition, three factors, capability-diversity tension）
- **P8 (实验范围)**: 不变
- **P9 (contributions)**: 重新措辞为 TTS lens：
  1. "Confidence signals as test-time scaling diagnostics" (QE + selective prediction)
  2. "Failure modes of test-time scaling for structured prediction" (degeneracy + LP compression diagnostic)
  3. "Entity-level aggregation as a structured test-time scaling strategy" (construction)

### 3. Related Work（29行 → ~31行，+2行预算）
**段落重组**：
- **P1 "Test-time compute scaling"（扩展主导段）**: 以 TTS 范式开篇。三条路径：(a) iterative reasoning (o1/o3, s1), (b) repeated sampling + voting (SC: Wang et al.), (c) repeated sampling + selection (BoN: Gao et al., Brown et al.; compute-optimal: Snell et al.)。所有路径假设 discrete/verifiable output。→ 引出我们的问题：structured output 怎么办？
- **P2 "Consistency for structured IE"**: 基本不变，重框为 "the only prior work connecting TTS to IE"
- **P3 "Uncertainty estimation and MBR"**: 不变
- **P4 "Best-of-N with learned verifiers"**: 不变，但强调 TTS 文献中 verifier 是关键——我们的诊断解释了为什么 unsupervised TTS 在 structured output 上失败，指向 verifier 作为解决方向

### 4. Discussion（10行 → 10行，等长）
- 最后一句增加 TTS 回扣："the selection window narrows with model improvement" → 加 "echoing the broader tension between model capability and test-time improvability identified in the TTS literature"
- 其他不变

### 5. Conclusion（3行 → 3行，等长）
- 增加 TTS 定位句替换现有 verifier 句："Our results delineate the boundary conditions for test-time compute scaling in structured prediction; content-aware verifiers may be needed to extend TTS gains beyond this boundary."

### 6. 不动的章节
- Method (§3): 不变——Problem Formulation 已自然覆盖 C2 (set-valued output)
- Experiments (§4): 按 Director 指令不动
- Appendix: 不动

### 7. C4 (SC-Bench)
- 在 Conclusion 或 Discussion 加一句 future work 提及："A standardized benchmark for test-time scaling on structured tasks (covering diverse output structures, degeneracy regimes, and verifier access) would accelerate progress."
- 若 Director 要求详细版本，可加 appendix subsection

## 页面预算分析

当前主文本恰好 8 页。改动策略：
- Introduction: +3行（通过压缩现有 P1+P2 合并为新 P1+P2 来腾出空间，净增 ≤3行）
- Related Work: +2行（TTS 段扩展 ~5行，压缩其他段 ~3行）
- Abstract/Discussion/Conclusion: 等长替换
- 总计净增 ~5行 ≈ 0.15 column，在 margin 内

## 新增引用

需要加入 .bib 的新条目（已验证真实）：
1. `muennighoff2025s1` — s1: Simple test-time scaling (EMNLP 2025)
2. o1/o3 — 如用 OpenAI blog 引用，需确认 cite key

已有可复用：`snell2025scaling`, `brown2024monkeys`, `wang2023selfconsistency`, `gao2023scaling`, `cobbe2021verifiers`

## 标题建议（供 Director 决策）

A. 保持现标题不变（"Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: ..."）— 已被 Reviewer 熟悉
B. "When Does Test-Time Scaling Work for Structured Prediction? The Correlation-Selection Gap in NER"
C. "Test-Time Compute Scaling Meets Structured Prediction: Diagnosing Failure Modes in Self-Consistency for NER"

建议 A（标题不变）+ Introduction/Abstract 加强 TTS framing，风险最低。标题改动由 Director 决定。

**3. 不要提 DGEC / signal-adaptive weighting**
论文中不要写入 DGEC 相关内容。VC/SJ-weighted construction 结果是 mixed/negative，暂不纳入主文叙事。如果后续 18 方向中有突破（B1 SCD, B2 Verifier），再 Patch。

Self-consistency (majority voting over multiple samples) yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}, and test-time compute scaling has emerged as a complementary axis to model scaling \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.

tool_args.new_string:
Test-time compute scaling---allocating additional inference-time computation to improve output quality---has emerged as a complement to model scaling \cite{snell2025scaling}. Repeated sampling with majority voting \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}, best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, brown2024monkeys}, and extended chain-of-thought \cite{muennighoff2025s1} yield large gains on reasoning, code generation, and mathematics, but the evidence concentrates on tasks where outputs admit equivalence classes or execution-based verification.
Named entity recognition (NER) poses a structurally different challenge: the output is a \textit{set} of entities, two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical sets, and there is no obvious majority to vote on.

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Self-consistency and test-time scaling.}
Self-consistency \cite{wang2023selfconsistency} improves reasoning via majority voting; extensions handle free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}.
Test-time scaling studies \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys} and reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} rely on answer-level agreement.
Adaptive variants gate on answer agreement \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive}, input difficulty \cite{wang2025make, feng2025optimal}, or response confidence \cite{kim2026reasc}; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose SC failure modes without proposing gating.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different gating signals because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive variants that gate on answer agreement \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive}, input difficulty \cite{wang2025make, feng2025optimal}, or response confidence \cite{kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.
